'''Jean-Philippe Bouchaud''' (born 1962) is a French [[physicist]]. He is co-founder and chairman of [[Capital Fund Management]] (CFM), adjunct professor at [[École Normale Supérieure]] and co-director of the CFM-Polytechnique Chair of [[Econophysics]] and Complex Systems at [[Ecole Polytechnique]]. He is a member of the [[Académie des Sciences|French Academy of Sciences]], and held the Bettencourt Innovation Chair at [[Collège de France]] in 2020. In 2026, he was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]].

== Biography ==
Born in [[Paris]] in 1962, Jean-Philippe Bouchaud studied at the French Lycée in London. Graduating from [[École Normale Supérieure]] in 1985, he carried out his PhD at the Laboratory of Hertzian Spectroscopy, studying spin-polarized quantum gases with Claire Lhuillier. He then worked for the [[French National Center for Scientific Research]], in particular on liquid Helium 3 and diffusion in random media. He spent a year at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]], [[University of Cambridge]] in 1992 before joining the Laboratory of Condensed Matter Physics (SPEC)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iramis.cea.fr/spec/ |title=Service de Physique de l'Etat Condensé |publisher=Iramis.cea.fr |date=2022-08-29 |access-date=2022-09-02}}</ref> of the French Atomic Energy and Alternative Energies Commission ([[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique]] or CEA)<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.cea.fr/ | title=Accueil - de la recherche à l'industrie| date=2013-10-19}}</ref> à [[Saclay]]. Pioneer in [[econophysics]], he co-founded the company Science et Finance in 1994, which later merged with [[Capital Fund Management]] (CFM)<ref>http://www.cfm.fr/us/organisation.php{{dead link|date=November 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> in 2000. He is now the Chairman of CFM. After teaching [[statistical mechanics]] for ten years at [[ESPCI]], he was appointed in 2009 as an adjunct Professor at [[École Polytechnique]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.physique.polytechnique.edu/home/faculty/faculty-members-28647.kjsp?RH=1252403432416 |title=École Polytechnique |access-date=2011-11-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120421010620/http://www.physique.polytechnique.edu/home/faculty/faculty-members-28647.kjsp?RH=1252403432416 |archive-date=2012-04-21 }}</ref> He now teaches a course ''From Statistical Mechanics to Social Sciences'' at [[École Normale Supérieure]] and, for a year, at [[Collège de France]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.college-de-france.fr/site/jean-philippe-bouchaud/inaugural-lecture-2020-2021.htm|title=De la physique statistique aux sciences sociales: les défis de la pluridisciplinarité|date=5 July 2019 }}</ref> His work covers the physics of disordered and glassy systems, granular materials, the statistics of price formation, stock market fluctuations and the modelling of [[financial risk]]s. He has repeatedly criticized the [[dogma]] of the [[efficient-market hypothesis]] and the [[methodology]] of economics and [[mathematical finance]],<ref>"Reliance on models based on incorrect axioms has clear and large effects. The Black–Scholes model for example, which was invented in 1973 to price options, is still used extensively. But it assumes that the probability of extreme price changes is negligible, when in reality, stock prices are much jerkier than this. Twenty years ago, unwarranted use of the model spiralled into the worldwide October 1987 crash; the Dow Jones index dropped 23% in a single day, dwarfing recent market hiccups." in [https://home.iitk.ac.in/~osegu/Nature.pdf "Economics needs a scientific revolution"]</ref> in particular the use of the [[Black–Scholes]] model which leads to a systematic underestimation of risk in [[Option (finance)|options trading]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cfm.fr/assets/ResearchPapers/2001-Welcome-to-a-non-Black-Scholes-world.pdf |title="Welcome to a non Black–Scholes world" |access-date=2020-05-29 |archive-date=2021-05-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210524151717/https://www.cfm.fr/assets/ResearchPapers/2001-Welcome-to-a-non-Black-Scholes-world.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Awards==
* [[IBM]] Young Researcher Prize in 1989<ref>[http://sfp.in2p3.fr/Prix/prix_anciens.html Prix IBM]</ref>
* [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 1995<ref>[http://www.cnrs.fr/cw/fr/nomi/prix/Argent95/argent95.html Médaille d'argent du CNRS] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090921013600/http://www.cnrs.fr/cw/fr/nomi/prix/Argent95/argent95.html |date=2009-09-21 }}</ref>
* ''[[Risk (magazine)|Risk]]'' Quant of the Year in 2017<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.risk.net/risk-magazine/analysis/2479713/quant-of-the-year-jean-philippe-bouchaud | title=Quant of the year: Jean-Philippe Bouchaud| date=2017-01-25}}</ref>
* Elected as member of the [[Académie des Sciences|French Academy of Sciences]] in 2017.
* Elected at the chaire Bettencourt de l'innovation at [[Collège de France]] in 2020.
* Quant Researcher of the Year, [[Journal of Portfolio Management]] in 2024.
* [[Lars Onsager Prize]] of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2025, together with [[Leticia Cugliandolo]] and [[Jorge Kurchan]] for their work on the dynamics of glassy systems.
